The most compelling evidence is [E21], which shows a discounted cash flow (DCF) putting intrinsic value at Rs 7 per share against a market price of Rs 465, indicating a margin of safety of -6265.2%. This stark discrepancy implies that the stock is overvalued by an extraordinary amount, suggesting that the current market price already discounts much more favorable future growth than what the base case assumes. [E43] further reinforces this point by highlighting a valuation blind-spot: Rich valuation — DCF overvalued 6265%. This warning underscores that a market-beating chart does not make a rich entry safe. The evidence clearly indicates that the stock is trading at an unsustainable premium, warranting caution and potential selling. In summary, [E21] and [E43] provide compelling evidence of overvaluation, leaving no room for support of the current valuation or recommendation to hold the stock.
